1. import { z } from "zod";
2. 
3. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
4. import type { ProjectValues } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
5. import type {
6.   StructuredBatchEntry,
7.   StructuredRequestContext,
8. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
9. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
10. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
11. import type { CreateAppointmentQuestion } from "@/types/scheduling/schedule";
12. 
13. /** The wire shape is already the row shape — no widening needed, so the
14.  *  `appointment` arm of `StructuredDataMap` (`structured/types.ts:42`) is
15.  *  untouched by this port. */
16. export type AppointmentRow = CreateAppointmentQuestion;
17. 
18. /**
19.  * Runtime guard on externally authored rows. Deliberately permissive on
20.  * `note`/`slot_id` — both may be legitimately blank mid-edit. A schema's
21.  * job is "is this a plausible row shape", not "is this row complete enough
22.  * to submit"; completeness is `needsSlot`'s separate, edit-log-aware
23.  * decision.
24.  */
25. export const rowSchema = z
26.   .object({
27.     note: z.string(),
28.     slot_id: z.string(),
29.     tags: z.array(z.string()),
30.   })
31.   .strict();
32. 
33. /**
34.  * Is `row.slot_id` a real slot address, not just a truthy string? A caller
35.  * that stringifies a missing id (`String(slot?.id)`) hands us the literal
36.  * `"undefined"`/`"null"` — truthy, and composing exactly the
37.  * `/slots/undefined/create_appointment/` URL this module exists to
38.  * prevent; whitespace is the same failure one step removed.
39.  *
40.  * THE ONE PREDICATE for "is a slot picked" — shared by `toRequests`,
41.  * `needsSlot` and `isEmptyRow`, so submission, validation and emptiness
42.  * can never disagree about what counts as a slot.
43.  */
44. function hasValidSlot(row: AppointmentRow | undefined): boolean {
45.   const slotId = row?.slot_id?.trim();
46.   return !!slotId && slotId !== "undefined" && slotId !== "null";
47. }
48. 
49. /** Clearing every field annihilates the `add`, so the section goes clean
50.  *  rather than sitting on an empty row that keeps the form dirty forever. */
51. export function isEmptyRow(row: AppointmentRow): boolean {
52.   return !row.note?.trim() && !hasValidSlot(row) && !row.tags?.length;
53. }
54. 
55. /**
56.  * PROJECTION vs VALIDATION vs SUBMISSION — three questions, three
57.  * predicates, reconciled deliberately. For the same row (a note typed, no
58.  * slot picked):
59.  *
60.  *  - PROJECTION (`isEmptyRow`) — a wholly blank row must not project (a
61.  *    non-empty value array reads as ANSWERED to `entryHasContent`, lighting
62.  *    the outline tick while submitting nothing), but a note-only row is
63.  *    real clinician input and MUST project.
64.  *  - VALIDATION (`needsSlot`) — a note-only row is content without a
65.  *    destination; the clinician must be told, not left to discover a quiet
66.  *    no-op after submit.
67.  *  - SUBMISSION (`hasValidSlot` in `toRequests`) — the slot is the address
68.  *    of the POST; no address, no request, however much other content the
69.  *    row carries: a stricter gate than `isEmptyRow`.
70.  *
71.  * The three never disagree in the direction that matters: a row that won't
72.  * submit either isn't projected at all, or projects AND trips `needsSlot`
73.  * — never projects clean while quietly submitting nothing. Each leg is
74.  * pinned by its own test.
75.  */
76. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<AppointmentRow> = (rows) => {
77.   // Singleton collapse: `rows` is `useStructuredRows`'s already-projected
78.   // baseline+edits set. `rows[0]` is exactly what `SingleRowController.row`
79.   // itself shows the editor (`useStructuredRows.ts:616`) — this must agree
80.   // with THAT, not spread every entry, even under a corrupted multi-rowId
81.   // log (see `resolveSingletonRow`'s doc comment for why `toRequests`
82.   // resolves the SAME position, not a rowId it filters for independently).
83.   const row = rows[0];
84.   if (!row || isEmptyRow(row)) return [];
85.   return [{ type: "appointment", value: [row] }];
86. };
87. 
88. /** `mode: "single"` with no baseline needs a complete row to record an
89.  *  `add` against — `patch` is always the whole row. Appointment is
90.  *  create-only: there is no server row to seed from, unlike `encounter`. */
91. export function createSeed(): AppointmentRow {
92.   return { note: "", slot_id: "", tags: [] };
93. }
94. 
95. /**
96.  * Resolves the edit log down to the one row this create-only singleton
97.  * holds, or `undefined`.
98.  *
99.  * Passes an explicit, KNOWN-EMPTY `baseline` — not `{}` (baseline
100.  * `undefined`, "not yet known"): a create-only singleton has no server
101.  * row, ever, so an `update`/`remove` for ANY rowId is an orphan by the
102.  * same rule `projectRows` applies, and only `creates` can hold anything.
103.  *
104.  * Do NOT pre-filter `edits` to a fixed singleton rowId: `projectValues`'
105.  * signature is bare `TRow[]` — it can only fall back to positional
106.  * `rows[0]` — so an identity filter here would make projection and
107.  * submission pick DIFFERENT rows under a corrupted multi-rowId log. Both
108.  * sides instead use the same signal, log order over the same empty
109.  * baseline, so `creates[0]` is `rows[0]` by construction — provided the
110.  * log has at most one entry per rowId, which every log produced by
111.  * `applyEditToLog` or surviving `sanitizeStructuredEditLog` does. A raw,
112.  * doubly-malformed log (duplicate entries for one rowId interleaved with
113.  * another's) can still diverge — executed and excluded in `model.test.ts`'s
114.  * sanitize-boundary cases, since every real ingestion path sanitizes
115.  * first.
116.  */
117. function resolveSingletonRow(
118.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<AppointmentRow>[],
119. ): AppointmentRow | undefined {
120.   const { creates } = resolveChanges(edits, { baseline: new Map() });
121.   return creates[0];
122. }
123. 
124. export async function toRequests(
125.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<AppointmentRow>[],
126.   { patientId, facilityId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
127. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
128.   if (!patientId || !facilityId) return [];
129.   const row = resolveSingletonRow(edits);
130.   // SUBMISSION gate (see `projectValues`). Appointment is create-only: the
131.   // slot is the whole address of the request, and composing the URL
132.   // without a valid one fails server-side — rolling back the entire atomic
133.   // batch, so a half-filled appointment would silently discard every other
134.   // section. No slot => no request, even though `row` may be real content;
135.   // `needsSlot` is what tells the clinician why nothing was booked.
136.   if (!row || !hasValidSlot(row)) return [];
137.   const slotId = row.slot_id.trim();
138.   return [
139.     {
140.       url: `/api/v1/facility/${facilityId}/slots/${slotId}/create_appointment/`,
141.       method: "POST",
142.       body: { note: row.note, patient: patientId, tags: row.tags },
143.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("appointment", questionId),
144.     },
145.   ];
146. }
147. 
148. /**
149.  * Is a slot mandatory right now? The VALIDATION half of the three-way
150.  * reconciliation on `projectValues`' doc comment: silently dropping a
151.  * slotless appointment (`toRequests`, above) is only safe if the clinician
152.  * is told. Two triggers:
153.  *  - the question is REQUIRED — an appointment is the answer, so it needs
154.  *    a slot regardless of what else is filled in;
155.  *  - the section was TOUCHED (`edits.length > 0`) and carries content
156.  *    other than a slot — a reason or tags with nowhere to book them.
157.  *    Today this passes validation and quietly books nothing.
158.  * Untouched and not required stays silent: an appointment section nobody
159.  * opened is not an error. `partiallyFilled` reads `projection[0]` — the
160.  * SAME positional row `toRequests`/`resolveSingletonRow` resolves to for a
161.  * well-formed log (see that function's doc comment) — so a log whose only
162.  * content is an orphaned edit (nothing survives to `projection[0]`) can
163.  * never trip this on content nobody can see: `partiallyFilled` is `false`
164.  * whenever `row` itself is `undefined`, independent of `edits.length`.
165.  * The message itself is added in the definition, at the i18n boundary —
166.  * this module must not import i18next.
167.  */
168. export function needsSlot(
169.   projection: readonly AppointmentRow[],
170.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<AppointmentRow>[],
171.   required: boolean,
172. ): boolean {
173.   const row = projection[0];
174.   if (hasValidSlot(row)) return false;
175.   if (required) return true;
176.   const partiallyFilled = !!row?.note?.trim() || !!row?.tags?.length;
177.   return partiallyFilled && edits.length > 0;
178. }
179.

1. import { z } from "zod";
2. 
3. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
4. import type { ProjectValues } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
5. import {
6.   displayObjectSchema,
7.   nonEmptyString,
8.   userDisplaySchema,
9. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/shared/rowSchemaPrimitives";
10. import type {
11.   StructuredBatchEntry,
12.   StructuredRequestContext,
13. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
14. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
15. import type {
16.   ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest,
17.   ChargeItemQuestionRow,
18. } from "@/types/billing/chargeItem/chargeItem";
19. import { ChargeItemServiceResource } from "@/types/billing/chargeItem/chargeItem";
20. import type { ChargeItemDefinitionRead } from "@/types/billing/chargeItemDefinition/chargeItemDefinition";
21. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
22. 
23. /**
24.  * The definition object is required here — every row the editor creates
25.  * comes from a picked `ChargeItemDefinitionRead` (`newChargeItemRow`) —
26.  * while the wider `ChargeItemQuestionRow` arm keeps both display objects
27.  * optional, since it also describes legacy responses and old drafts where
28.  * they may be absent.
29.  */
30. export type ChargeItemRow = ChargeItemQuestionRow & {
31.   charge_item_definition_object: ChargeItemDefinitionRead;
32. };
33. 
34. /**
35.  * Assistant write guard. `charge_item_definition_object`/
36.  * `performer_actor_object` are passthrough, id-keyed-only schemas: an
37.  * assistant only ever copies one verbatim from a prior pick, never authors
38.  * the full `ChargeItemDefinitionRead`/`UserReadMinimal` shape by hand. Every
39.  * other field is `.strict()`.
40.  */
41. export const rowSchema = z
42.   .object({
43.     charge_item_definition: nonEmptyString,
44.     quantity: z.string(),
45.     encounter: z.string().optional(),
46.     patient: z.string().optional(),
47.     service_resource: z.enum(ChargeItemServiceResource).optional(),
48.     service_resource_id: z.string().optional(),
49.     performer_actor: z.string().optional(),
50.     account: z.string().optional(),
51.     charge_item_definition_object: displayObjectSchema(["slug", "title"]),
52.     performer_actor_object: userDisplaySchema.optional(),
53.   })
54.   .strict();
55. 
56. /**
57.  * A charge-item section is a LIST whose rows are born whole
58.  * (`newChargeItemRow`): there is no "half filled" state, so no `isEmptyRow`
59.  * predicate to keep in sync with a submission filter. Whatever `rows` holds
60.  * is what the clinician sees and exactly the set `toRequests` compiles
61.  * requests for.
62.  */
63. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<ChargeItemRow> = (rows) =>
64.   rows.length === 0 ? [] : [{ type: "charge_item", value: [...rows] }];
65. 
66. /**
67.  * A freshly picked definition becomes a row: quantity defaults to `"1"`,
68.  * `encounter` comes from context (a charge item is always billed to the
69.  * encounter being filled), and the definition's `slug` is the wire identity
70.  * `apply_charge_item_defs/` expects. The definition object rides along on
71.  * the row — not fetched a second time — so a restored draft or the list can
72.  * repaint title/price straight from the response.
73.  */
74. export function newChargeItemRow(
75.   definition: ChargeItemDefinitionRead,
76.   encounterId: string,
77. ): ChargeItemRow {
78.   return {
79.     quantity: "1",
80.     encounter: encounterId,
81.     charge_item_definition: definition.slug,
82.     charge_item_definition_object: definition,
83.   };
84. }
85. 
86. /**
87.  * The single place display objects are stripped before the wire. The exact
88.  * remaining key set is pinned by a dedicated test, not inferred from this
89.  * comment.
90.  */
91. export function stripDisplay(
92.   row: ChargeItemRow,
93. ): ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest {
94.   const {
95.     charge_item_definition_object: _definition,
96.     performer_actor_object: _performer,
97.     ...request
98.   } = row;
99.   return request;
100. }
101. 
102. export async function toRequests(
103.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<ChargeItemRow>[],
104.   { facilityId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
105. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
106.   if (!facilityId) return [];
107.   // Create-only: no server row is ever fetched for this type, so the baseline
108.   // is permanently empty — stated as an explicit empty Map because omitting
109.   // `baseline` means "still loading or errored" per
110.   // `ResolveChangesOptions.baseline`, which is not the fact here.
111.   //
112.   // `updates`/`removes` are deliberately not merged into the request body:
113.   // `apply_charge_item_defs/` is create-only (no verb for an update), and a
114.   // remove for a rowId that never reached the server carries nothing worth
115.   // sending. Add-then-remove pairs annihilate inside the reducer before this
116.   // function ever sees them.
117.   const { creates } = resolveChanges(edits, { baseline: new Map() });
118.   if (creates.length === 0) return [];
119.   return [
120.     {
121.       url: `/api/v1/facility/${facilityId}/charge_item/apply_charge_item_defs/`,
122.       method: "POST",
123.       body: { requests: creates.map(stripDisplay) },
124.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("charge_item", questionId),
125.     },
126.   ];
127. }
128. 
129. /** Is `quantity` a positive integer, written as the wire's plain string
130.  *  (`ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest.quantity: string`)? Trimmed first so
131.  *  incidental whitespace doesn't fail a value that is otherwise a clean
132.  *  integer — the same defensive trim `appointment`'s `hasValidSlot` applies
133.  *  to `slot_id`. `"0"`/negative values fail the `>= 1` check, not the regex,
134.  *  so both are reported for the same reason a clinician can act on: not a
135.  *  quantity, not "at least one". */
136. function isPositiveIntegerQuantity(quantity: string): boolean {
137.   const trimmed = quantity.trim();
138.   return /^\d+$/.test(trimmed) && Number(trimmed) >= 1;
139. }
140. 
141. /**
142.  * Row-scoped quantity predicate; the definition's `validate()` turns each
143.  * returned rowId into a blocking `QuestionValidationError`. The wire type is
144.  * a bare string (`ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest.quantity`) and the
145.  * editor's `<Input type="number" min={1}>` is only a browser hint, so
146.  * `""`/`"-1"`/`"abc"` are all representable — this predicate is the only
147.  * client-side gate.
148.  *
149.  * `toRequests` deliberately does NOT also filter on it: client validation
150.  * runs before request compilation and blocks the whole submit on any error,
151.  * so `toRequests` cannot run while an invalid quantity survives — and having
152.  * it silently drop the row instead would make the clinician's entry vanish
153.  * from the request with no message they can act on. Projection and submit
154.  * therefore both include a row regardless of its quantity's validity.
155.  *
156.  * A `remove` edit's quantity is never reported: the row is on its way out,
157.  * not something the clinician still needs to fix.
158.  */
159. export function invalidQuantityRowIds(
160.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<ChargeItemRow>[],
161. ): string[] {
162.   return edits
163.     .filter(
164.       (edit) =>
165.         edit.op !== "remove" && !isPositiveIntegerQuantity(edit.patch.quantity),
166.     )
167.     .map((edit) => edit.rowId);
168. }
169.

3. 
4. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
5. import type {
6.   BaselineRow,
7.   ProjectValues,
8.   SoftDeleteDescriptor,
9. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
10. import {
11.   onsetSchema,
12.   userDisplaySchema,
13. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/shared/rowSchemaPrimitives";
14. import type {
15.   StructuredBatchEntry,
16.   StructuredRequestContext,
17. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
18. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
19. import { CodeSchema, type Code } from "@/types/base/code/code";
20. import type {
21.   Diagnosis,
22.   DiagnosisRequest,
23. } from "@/types/emr/diagnosis/diagnosis";
24. import {
25.   DIAGNOSIS_CATEGORY,
26.   DIAGNOSIS_CLINICAL_STATUS,
27.   DIAGNOSIS_SEVERITY,
28.   DIAGNOSIS_VERIFICATION_STATUS,
29. } from "@/types/emr/diagnosis/diagnosis";
30. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
31. 
32. /** The wire request shape doubles as the editable row shape. */
33. export type DiagnosisRow = DiagnosisRequest;
34. 
35. /**
36.  * Assistant write guard. `severity` is `.nullable()` to match
37.  * `DiagnosisRequest.severity: DiagnosisSeverity | null`. Timestamp fields
38.  * are read-only pass-through, left as plain optional strings.
39.  */
40. export const rowSchema = z
41.   .object({
42.     id: z.string().optional(),
43.     clinical_status: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_CLINICAL_STATUS),
44.     verification_status: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_VERIFICATION_STATUS),
45.     code: CodeSchema,
46.     severity: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_SEVERITY).nullable(),
47.     onset: onsetSchema.optional(),
48.     recorded_date: z.string().optional(),
49.     note: z.string().optional(),
50.     category: z.enum(DIAGNOSIS_CATEGORY),
51.     encounter: z.string().min(1),
52.     created_by: userDisplaySchema.optional(),
53.     created_date: z.string().optional(),
54.     updated_date: z.string().optional(),
55.   })
56.   .strict();
57. 
58. /**
59.  * Removing a row that exists on the server flips `verification_status` to
60.  * `entered_in_error` and keeps it visible; a row that never reached the
61.  * server is dropped outright. `useStructuredRows` dispatches on this
62.  * descriptor by row origin.
63.  */
64. export const DIAGNOSIS_SOFT_DELETE: SoftDeleteDescriptor<DiagnosisRow> = {
65.   patch: { verification_status: "entered_in_error" },
66.   isDeleted: (row) => row.verification_status === "entered_in_error",
67. };
68. 
69. /**
70.  * Read shape → the row this question edits; `onset.onset_datetime` is cut
71.  * down to a bare date. Uses `date-fns` directly — `@/Utils/utils`
72.  * transitively reads `import.meta.env` via `@careConfig`, undefined under
73.  * `node --test`.
74.  */
75. export function toDiagnosisRow(diagnosis: Diagnosis): DiagnosisRow {
76.   return {
77.     id: diagnosis.id,
78.     code: diagnosis.code,
79.     clinical_status: diagnosis.clinical_status,
80.     verification_status: diagnosis.verification_status,
81.     severity: diagnosis.severity,
82.     onset: diagnosis.onset
83.       ? {
84.           ...diagnosis.onset,
85.           onset_datetime: diagnosis.onset.onset_datetime
86.             ? format(new Date(diagnosis.onset.onset_datetime), "yyyy-MM-dd")
87.             : "",
88.         }
89.       : undefined,
90.     recorded_date: diagnosis.recorded_date,
91.     category: diagnosis.category,
92.     note: diagnosis.note,
93.     encounter: diagnosis.encounter,
94.     created_by: diagnosis.created_by,
95.     created_date: diagnosis.created_date,
96.   };
97. }
98. 
99. /**
100.  * Keyed by the server id so `removeRow` distinguishes baseline
101.  * (soft-delete) from added (annihilate) rows. Callers pass `undefined`,
102.  * never `[]`, while the fetch is unresolved.
103.  */
104. export function toBaselineRows(
105.   diagnoses: readonly Diagnosis[],
106. ): BaselineRow<DiagnosisRow>[] {
107.   return diagnoses.map((diagnosis) => ({
108.     rowId: diagnosis.id,
109.     row: toDiagnosisRow(diagnosis),
110.   }));
111. }
112. 
113. /**
114.  * Legacy add-flow defaults: active/confirmed, severity "moderate",
115.  * category "encounter_diagnosis", onset today. Only the historical-record
116.  * flow can bring in a "chronic_condition" row. `encounter` is set at
117.  * creation because a row's `patch` must be the complete row.
118.  */
119. export function newDiagnosisRow(code: Code, encounterId: string): DiagnosisRow {
120.   return {
121.     code,
122.     clinical_status: "active",
123.     verification_status: "confirmed",
124.     severity: "moderate",
125.     category: "encounter_diagnosis",
126.     onset: { onset_datetime: format(new Date(), "yyyy-MM-dd") },
127.     encounter: encounterId,
128.   };
129. }
130. 
131. /** Rows are complete from creation — no empty-row filter needed; an
132.  *  empty list projects to an unanswered section. */
133. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<DiagnosisRow> = (rows) =>
134.   rows.length === 0 ? [] : [{ type: "diagnosis", value: [...rows] }];
135. 
136. /** Duplicate-guard key for `findDuplicateCandidates`, which already
137.  *  excludes soft-deleted (entered_in_error) rows from its seen set. */
138. export function diagnosisDuplicateKey(row: DiagnosisRow): string | undefined {
139.   return row.code.code || undefined;
140. }
141. 
142. function onsetTime(row: DiagnosisRow): number {
143.   // A missing onset gets a fixed rank (sorts last): the comparator must
144.   // be pure and deterministic, so no wall-clock fallback.
145.   return row.onset?.onset_datetime
146.     ? new Date(row.onset.onset_datetime).getTime()
147.     : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
148. }
149. 
150. /**
151.  * Display-only onset-ascending sort, passed as `displayOrder` to
152.  * `projectRows`: it reorders the returned `ProjectedRow[]` only. The
153.  * baseline and edit log — and therefore `toRequests` — never see this
154.  * order; rows are addressed by `rowId`, never by position.
155.  */
156. export function diagnosisDisplayOrder(
157.   a: DiagnosisRow,
158.   b: DiagnosisRow,
159. ): number {
160.   return onsetTime(a) - onsetTime(b);
161. }
162. 
163. /**
164.  * Onset is frozen once a row exists on the server — editing a recorded
165.  * diagnosis's onset would rewrite clinical history. A row re-added from
166.  * history has its id stripped and is genuinely new, so its onset stays
167.  * editable.
168.  */
169. export function isOnsetFrozen(origin: "baseline" | "added"): boolean {
170.   return origin === "baseline";
171. }
172. 
173. /** Kept local rather than importing `definitions/adapt.ts`'s
174.  *  `sanitizeNote`: `model.ts` must stay React-free for `node --test`, and
175.  *  adapt.ts imports React. */
176. function sanitizeNote(note: string | undefined): string | undefined {
177.   return note?.trim() || undefined;
178. }
179. 
180. /**
181.  * Reuses a historical diagnosis as a NEW row for this encounter: the
182.  * server id is stripped — keeping it would make the upsert update the
183.  * original record in place — a null severity defaults to "moderate", and
184.  * `encounter` is re-stamped to the current encounter.
185.  */
186. export function toReusedDiagnosisRow(
187.   row: DiagnosisRow,
188.   encounterId: string,
189. ): DiagnosisRow {
190.   const { id: _id, ...rest } = row;
191.   return {
192.     ...rest,
193.     severity: rest.severity ?? "moderate",
194.     encounter: encounterId,
195.   };
196. }
197. 
198. /**
199.  * Edit log → at most one POST to the upsert endpoint. An empty edit log
200.  * yields an empty batch — dirtiness is derived from the log, so untouched
201.  * baseline rows are never re-sent.
202.  *
203.  * `resolveChanges` receives no baseline: the differ only sees the edit
204.  * log, and the hook's prune effect drops edits for rows the baseline has
205.  * proven gone before submit. A `removes` entry always carries `.row` when
206.  * a softDelete descriptor is supplied; the `flatMap` guard honors the
207.  * shared optional type instead of asserting.
208.  *
209.  * `encounter: encounterId` overrides each row's own value on purpose — a
210.  * historical row carries the encounter it was originally recorded under;
211.  * re-stamping attaches it to the current encounter (legacy submit
212.  * behavior).
213.  */
214. export async function toRequests(
215.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<DiagnosisRow>[],
216.   { patientId, encounterId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
217. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
218.   if (!patientId || !encounterId) return [];
219.   const { creates, updates, removes } = resolveChanges(edits, {
220.     softDelete: DIAGNOSIS_SOFT_DELETE,
221.   });
222.   const rows = [
223.     ...creates,
224.     ...updates,
225.     ...removes.flatMap((entry) => (entry.row ? [entry.row] : [])),
226.   ];
227.   if (rows.length === 0) return [];
228.   return [
229.     {
230.       url: `/api/v1/patient/${patientId}/diagnosis/upsert/`,
231.       method: "POST",
232.       body: {
233.         datapoints: rows.map((row) => ({
234.           ...row,
235.           note: sanitizeNote(row.note),
236.           encounter: encounterId,
237.         })),
238.       },
239.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("diagnosis", questionId),
240.     },
241.   ];
242. }
243.

1. import { z } from "zod";
2. 
3. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
4. import type {
5.   BaselineRow,
6.   ProjectValues,
7. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
8. import { periodSchema } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/shared/rowSchemaPrimitives";
9. import type {
10.   StructuredBatchEntry,
11.   StructuredRequestContext,
12. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
13. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
14. import {
15.   ENCOUNTER_ADMIT_SOURCE,
16.   ENCOUNTER_CLASS,
17.   ENCOUNTER_DIET_PREFERENCE,
18.   ENCOUNTER_DISCHARGE_DISPOSITION,
19.   ENCOUNTER_PRIORITY,
20.   EncounterStatus,
21.   type EncounterClass,
22.   type EncounterDischargeDisposition,
23.   type EncounterEdit,
24.   type EncounterRead,
25. } from "@/types/emr/encounter/encounter";
26. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
27. 
28. /**
29.  * `EncounterEdit` carries no `id` of its own — the only endpoint that
30.  * consumes it is URL-keyed (`PUT /api/v1/encounter/{id}/`). That fact
31.  * drives {@link toBaselineRows}'s rowId, {@link toRequests}' identity
32.  * filter, and why an `add` and an `update` compile to the same request.
33.  */
34. export type EncounterRow = EncounterEdit;
35. 
36. /** `Hospitalization`'s zod mirror — `.strict()`, every field optional,
37.  *  matching `Hospitalization`'s own four fields exactly. */
38. const hospitalizationSchema = z
39.   .object({
40.     re_admission: z.boolean().optional(),
41.     admit_source: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_ADMIT_SOURCE).optional(),
42.     discharge_disposition: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_DISCHARGE_DISPOSITION).optional(),
43.     diet_preference: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_DIET_PREFERENCE).optional(),
44.   })
45.   .strict();
46. 
47. /**
48.  * Runtime guard on externally authored rows. `hospitalization` accepts
49.  * `null`, matching `Hospitalization | null | undefined` — the server holds
50.  * `null` for an encounter that never had one. `external_identifier`/
51.  * `discharge_summary_advice` are `string | null` on the real type — both
52.  * `.nullable()`, not merely `.optional()`.
53.  */
54. export const rowSchema = z
55.   .object({
56.     status: z.enum(EncounterStatus),
57.     encounter_class: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_CLASS),
58.     period: periodSchema,
59.     hospitalization: hospitalizationSchema.nullable().optional(),
60.     priority: z.enum(ENCOUNTER_PRIORITY),
61.     external_identifier: z.string().nullable(),
62.     discharge_summary_advice: z.string().nullable(),
63.   })
64.   .strict();
65. 
66. /** Statuses that END an encounter, and therefore want a `period.end`. */
67. const TERMINAL_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<EncounterStatus> = new Set([
68.   EncounterStatus.DISCHARGED,
69.   EncounterStatus.COMPLETED,
70.   EncounterStatus.CANCELLED,
71.   EncounterStatus.DISCONTINUED,
72.   EncounterStatus.ENTERED_IN_ERROR,
73. ]);
74. 
75. /** Classes with no hospitalization record at all. */
76. const AMBULATORY_CLASSES: readonly EncounterClass[] = ["amb", "vr", "hh"];
77. 
78. /** Classes that DO carry one, and therefore need a discharge disposition
79.  *  once discharged. */
80. const HOSPITALIZED_CLASSES: readonly EncounterClass[] = [
81.   "imp",
82.   "obsenc",
83.   "emer",
84. ];
85. 
86. /**
87.  * Does this class carry a hospitalization record? The single authority for
88.  * this split — the editor's hospitalization panel, the derivation rules
89.  * and the validator must never disagree about which classes have one.
90.  */
91. export function isHospitalizedClass(encounterClass: EncounterClass): boolean {
92.   return HOSPITALIZED_CLASSES.includes(encounterClass);
93. }
94. 
95. /**
96.  * `EncounterRead` → the seven fields this question edits. Everything else
97.  * `EncounterRead` carries (patient, facility, tags, care team, histories,
98.  * permissions) is display data that must never ride along into a PUT
99.  * body; the exact key set is pinned by a test.
100.  */
101. export function toEncounterRow(read: EncounterRead): EncounterRow {
102.   return {
103.     status: read.status,
104.     encounter_class: read.encounter_class,
105.     period: read.period,
106.     hospitalization: read.hospitalization,
107.     priority: read.priority,
108.     external_identifier: read.external_identifier,
109.     discharge_summary_advice: read.discharge_summary_advice,
110.   };
111. }
112. 
113. /**
114.  * Exactly one baseline row, keyed by the ENCOUNTER id — not
115.  * `SINGLETON_ROW_ID`, which `core/rowIds.ts` reserves for create-only
116.  * types with no server row. This row's identity is the encounter id in the
117.  * PUT URL; keying the baseline by it lets {@link toRequests} decide from
118.  * the edit log alone whether an edit is about THIS encounter.
119.  *
120.  * Only ever called with a resolved `EncounterRead`, so the returned set is
121.  * complete. While the query is loading or errored the caller must pass
122.  * `undefined` to the hook, never `[]` — an empty array claims the server
123.  * has no rows, which reclassifies edits as data-creating and makes
124.  * `projectRows` drop every restored edit as an orphan.
125.  */
126. export function toBaselineRows(
127.   read: EncounterRead,
128.   encounterId: string,
129. ): BaselineRow<EncounterRow>[] {
130.   return [{ rowId: encounterId, row: toEncounterRow(read) }];
131. }
132. 
133. /**
134.  * Deliberately `rows[0]`, not `[...rows]`: `SingleRowController.row` hands
135.  * the editor exactly `rows[0]`, so a corrupted two-rowId log must not
136.  * project TWO encounters into `values[0].value` while the editor shows one
137.  * and {@link toRequests} PUTs one.
138.  *
139.  * No `isEmptyRow`: an encounter row always has a status, class, period and
140.  * priority — there is no blank state to clear it to. An untouched section
141.  * is silent because its EDIT LOG is empty, which {@link toRequests} checks
142.  * first.
143.  */
144. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<EncounterRow> = (rows) => {
145.   const row = rows[0];
146.   if (!row) return [];
147.   return [{ type: "encounter", value: [row] }];
148. };
149. 
150. /**
151.  * The encounter's domain derivations, one pure function applied to every
152.  * patch before it is recorded; a combined class+status edit is evaluated
153.  * against the values it is SETTING, and the one-pass fixpoint is executed
154.  * in `model.test.ts`.
155.  *
156.  * RETURN CONTRACT (`StructuredRowsOptions.normalizePatch`): the result
157.  * REPLACES `patch` before being spread onto the row, so it must start from
158.  * `{ ...patch }`. Takes its config rather than importing `@careConfig`
159.  * (`care.config.ts` reads `import.meta.env`, absent under `node --test`);
160.  * `now` is injectable so period assertions can name a value.
161.  *
162.  * Rules, in order:
163.  *  1. period.end follows the status — a terminal status with no end gets
164.  *     `now()`; an existing end is kept (a clinician-picked date is not
165.  *     re-stamped); a non-terminal status clears it, writing nothing when
166.  *     there is nothing to clear, so an unrelated edit cannot manufacture a
167.  *     period diff.
168.  *  2. An ambulatory class clears a POPULATED hospitalization to `{}` —
169.  *     never writes `{}` over a server `null`/already-`{}`, which would put
170.  *     an untouched field into the PUT body.
171.  *  3. A hospitalized class that is DISCHARGED gets a disposition — the one
172.  *     set, or the configured default.
173.  *
174.  * Deliberately NO rule re-pins `discharge_disposition` to the server value
175.  * on unrelated edits (that erased the clinician's pick mid-form); pinned
176.  * by a regression test.
177.  */
178. export function makeNormalizePatch({
179.   dischargeDisposition,
180.   now = () => new Date().toISOString(),
181. }: {
182.   // `| undefined`, matching `careConfig.defaultDischargeDisposition` (the
183.   // env var behind it is optional). Rule 3's `??` then leaves the
184.   // disposition unset — onto the itself-optional field — exactly the
185.   // behavior when no default is configured.
186.   dischargeDisposition: EncounterDischargeDisposition | undefined;
187.   now?: () => string;
188. }) {
189.   return function normalizePatch(
190.     row: EncounterRow,
191.     patch: Partial<EncounterRow>,
192.   ): Partial<EncounterRow> {
193.     const next = { ...row, ...patch };
194.     const out: Partial<EncounterRow> = { ...patch };
195. 
196.     // Rule 1 — period.end follows the status.
197.     if (TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(next.status)) {
198.       if (!next.period.end) out.period = { ...next.period, end: now() };
199.     } else if (next.period.end) {
200.       // `end: undefined` rather than a delete: `deepEqualJson` treats an
201.       // undefined-valued key as ABSENT, so this still collapses back to a
202.       // baseline that never had an end.
203.       out.period = { ...next.period, end: undefined };
204.     }
205. 
206.     // Rules 2 and 3 — the hospitalization record follows class + status.
207.     if (AMBULATORY_CLASSES.includes(next.encounter_class)) {
208.       if (
209.         next.hospitalization &&
210.         Object.keys(next.hospitalization).length > 0
211.       ) {
212.         out.hospitalization = {};
213.       }
214.     } else if (
215.       isHospitalizedClass(next.encounter_class) &&
216.       next.status === EncounterStatus.DISCHARGED
217.     ) {
218.       out.hospitalization = {
219.         ...next.hospitalization,
220.         discharge_disposition:
221.           next.hospitalization?.discharge_disposition ?? dischargeDisposition,
222.       };
223.     }
224. 
225.     return out;
226.   };
227. }
228. 
229. /**
230.  * Is a discharge disposition mandatory: a DISCHARGED encounter of a
231.  * hospitalized class with no disposition set. The definition turns this
232.  * into a `QuestionValidationError` on
233.  * `hospitalization.discharge_disposition`; the message lives there, at the
234.  * i18n boundary — this module must not import i18next.
235.  *
236.  * Where `careConfig.defaultDischargeDisposition` is unconfigured (the env
237.  * var is optional; this repo's `.env.local` does not set it),
238.  * {@link makeNormalizePatch}'s rule 3 leaves the field unset, so rows this
239.  * editor produces ("Mark for discharge", the `?toDischarge` seed) DO fail
240.  * this predicate — live required-field enforcement, Save blocks until a
241.  * value is picked. Only with a configured default does it degrade to a
242.  * safety net for rows nobody edited this session.
243.  */
244. export function requiresDischargeDisposition(
245.   row: EncounterRow | undefined,
246. ): boolean {
247.   return (
248.     row?.status === EncounterStatus.DISCHARGED &&
249.     isHospitalizedClass(row.encounter_class) &&
250.     !row.hospitalization?.discharge_disposition
251.   );
252. }
253. 
254. /**
255.  * Whether the missing-disposition error may block Save. An untouched
256.  * section may NOT: `edits.length > 0` is an unconditional precondition,
257.  * regardless of the question's own `required` flag — unlike
258.  * `appointment`'s `needsSlot`, which hard-blocks a required question even
259.  * untouched. Blocking Save over server data the clinician never brought
260.  * into the session would be a new coupling; `toRequests`' first guard
261.  * already guarantees an untouched section produces zero requests, and this
262.  * extends the same guarantee to validation.
263.  */
264. export function blocksSaveForMissingDischargeDisposition(
265.   row: EncounterRow | undefined,
266.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<EncounterRow>[],
267. ): boolean {
268.   return edits.length > 0 && requiresDischargeDisposition(row);
269. }
270. 
271. /**
272.  * The edit log → at most one `PUT /api/v1/encounter/{encounterId}/`. An
273.  * empty log means an empty batch — an untouched section must never PUT the
274.  * encounter back over whatever another user changed meanwhile.
275.  *
276.  * IDENTITY, NOT POSITION — unlike `appointment`'s `resolveSingletonRow`,
277.  * which cannot filter by rowId: the encounter's rowId IS the URL this
278.  * request is addressed to, and the baseline holds exactly this rowId, so
279.  * filtering to `rowId === encounterId` agrees with `projectRows` even
280.  * under a duplicate-entry log (a log carrying only a corrupted foreign
281.  * rowId sends nothing, matching the untouched row the projection shows).
282.  * The one precondition — the baseline is keyed by the same id this context
283.  * carries — is pinned by the "KNOWN GAP" test.
284.  *
285.  * `resolveChanges(own, {})` passes no baseline: the encounter's baseline
286.  * exists but is not available to a pure differ; `undefined` is the
287.  * contract's word for "not known". After the identity filter
288.  * `resolveChanges` dedups to at most one entry, so `updates[0] ??
289.  * creates[0]` is an exact pick; an `add` (recorded before the baseline
290.  * query resolved) compiles to the same PUT, safe because the endpoint is
291.  * URL-keyed. `removes` is dropped: this question has no delete verb, and
292.  * `projectRows` hides a `remove`d baseline row, so an empty projection and
293.  * an empty batch agree.
294.  *
295.  * The body stays the seven-field allowlist — deliberately not widened to
296.  * the whole row.
297.  */
298. export async function toRequests(
299.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<EncounterRow>[],
300.   { encounterId, facilityId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
301. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
302.   if (edits.length === 0) return [];
303.   if (!encounterId) return [];
304.   if (!facilityId) {
305.     // A mount precondition, not a URL ingredient — `requires:
306.     // ["encounterId", "facilityId"]` means the question should never have
307.     // rendered without one. A throw rather than a silent `[]` so the
308.     // failure is loud; `composeBatch` contains it as a question-scoped
309.     // `StructuredBuildError`. It is checked AFTER the empty-log guard on
310.     // purpose: an untouched section must stay silent rather than fail the
311.     // whole submit.
312.     throw new Error("Cannot update an encounter without a facility");
313.   }
314. 
315.   const own = edits.filter((edit) => edit.rowId === encounterId);
316.   if (own.length === 0) return [];
317. 
318.   const { creates, updates } = resolveChanges(own, {});
319.   const row = updates[0] ?? creates[0];
320.   if (!row) return [];
321. 
322.   return [
323.     {
324.       url: `/api/v1/encounter/${encounterId}/`,
325.       method: "PUT",
326.       body: {
327.         status: row.status,
328.         encounter_class: row.encounter_class,
329.         period: row.period,
330.         hospitalization: row.hospitalization,
331.         priority: row.priority,
332.         external_identifier: row.external_identifier,
333.         discharge_summary_advice: row.discharge_summary_advice,
334.       },
335.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("encounter", questionId),
336.     },
337.   ];
338. }
339.

1. import { z } from "zod";
2. 
3. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
4. import type { ProjectValues } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
5. import type {
6.   StructuredBatchEntry,
7.   StructuredRequestContext,
8. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
9. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
10. import type { FileUploadQuestion } from "@/types/files/file";
11. import { FileCategory, FileType } from "@/types/files/file";
12. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
13. 
14. /**
15.  * Assistant write guard. `file_data: z.instanceof(File)` means this schema
16.  * ALWAYS rejects an assistant-authored patch by construction: an assistant
17.  * write arrives as plain JSON (`ApplyStructuredEditInput.patch: unknown`),
18.  * and a real browser `File` cannot be reconstructed from JSON — the same
19.  * round-trip impossibility behind this type's `draftPolicy: "exclude"`.
20.  * `File` is a Node/browser global, so `z.instanceof(File)` behaves the same
21.  * under `node --test` (Node 20+) as in the app.
22.  */
23. export const rowSchema = z
24.   .object({
25.     name: z.string(),
26.     file_type: z.enum(FileType),
27.     file_category: z.enum(FileCategory),
28.     associating_id: z.string().min(1),
29.     original_name: z.string().min(1),
30.     file_data: z.instanceof(File),
31.   })
32.   .strict();
33. 
34. /**
35.  * Carries `file_data: File` — a live browser handle, not plain data —
36.  * which is why `files` is `draftPolicy: "exclude"`: a `File` cannot be
37.  * `JSON.stringify`d into a draft, and even base64-encoded bytes could not
38.  * be turned back into a `File` on restore. No alternative row shape both
39.  * round-trips through a draft and still carries the file to upload.
40.  */
41. export type FileUploadRow = FileUploadQuestion;
42. 
43. /**
44.  * `name` starts EMPTY on purpose — the clinician has to type one.
45.  * `original_name` is the file's own name; `associating_id` is the encounter
46.  * this section is filling. `file_data` holds `file` BY REFERENCE, not a
47.  * copy — the same reference `toRequests` later hands to `readFileAsDataURL`.
48.  * This row is the only place a `File` lives between pick and submit: the
49.  * picker's buffer is drained into rows and cleared in the same tick
50.  * (`FilesEditor.tsx`'s effect), so there is only one store to read, update
51.  * or remove from.
52.  */
53. export function newFileRow(file: File, encounterId: string): FileUploadRow {
54.   return {
55.     name: "",
56.     file_data: file,
57.     original_name: file.name,
58.     file_type: FileType.ENCOUNTER,
59.     file_category: FileCategory.UNSPECIFIED,
60.     associating_id: encounterId,
61.   };
62. }
63. 
64. /**
65.  * A LIST with no "half filled" row: a row is born whole the moment
66.  * `newFileRow` creates it (its `name` starts `""`, but a `File` is already
67.  * attached). Deliberately no `isEmptyRow` filtering unnamed rows out of the
68.  * projection — projection and submit must agree, and `toRequests` submits
69.  * every surviving row regardless of `name`, trusting the blocking
70.  * `validate()` error (`unnamedFileRowIds`) to stop the submit first.
71.  * Filtering here would let an attached-but-unnamed file silently vanish
72.  * from both the screen and the request with no error at all.
73.  */
74. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<FileUploadRow> = (rows) =>
75.   rows.length === 0 ? [] : [{ type: "files", value: [...rows] }];
76. 
77. /**
78.  * Row-scoped, pure, i18n-free — the definition file turns this into a
79.  * translated `QuestionValidationError` per row. Only `name` is checked:
80.  * `file_data` and `original_name` come from the picked `File` itself and
81.  * cannot go blank the way the typed `name` can. Trimmed so pure whitespace
82.  * does not pass. A `remove` edit is never reported: the row is on its way
83.  * out, not something the clinician still needs to name.
84.  */
85. export function unnamedFileRowIds(
86.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<FileUploadRow>[],
87. ): string[] {
88.   return edits
89.     .filter((edit) => edit.op !== "remove" && !edit.patch.name?.trim())
90.     .map((edit) => edit.rowId);
91. }
92. 
93. /** The one dependency `toRequests` needs beyond `edits`/`context` —
94.  *  injected by `definitions/files.tsx`, deliberately never imported here
95.  *  (see `makeToRequests`). */
96. export interface FileRequestDeps {
97.   /** Turns a `File` into a `data:` URL. In production this is the real
98.    *  `readFileAsDataURL` (`@/Utils/utils`), wired in by `definitions/
99.    *  files.tsx` — never imported here directly. */
100.   readFileAsDataURL: (file: File) => Promise<string>;
101. }
102. 
103. /**
104.  * Files are uploaded, never amended or re-fetched: `creates` is the whole
105.  * story. `updates`/`removes` are not read — a well-formed log for this
106.  * create-only type only ever emits `add`, and there is no PATCH or delete
107.  * endpoint this differ could act on either way. An empty edit log produces
108.  * zero requests by construction.
109.  *
110.  * Base64 conversion happens HERE, in the differ, and nowhere else: the row
111.  * carries the live `File` right up to submission, so nothing upstream ever
112.  * holds a serialized form a draft could persist.
113.  *
114.  * `readFileAsDataURL` is injected (`FileRequestDeps`) rather than imported:
115.  * `@/Utils/utils` imports `@careConfig`, which reads `import.meta.env` at
116.  * module scope — `undefined` under `node --test` — so the import alone would
117.  * crash the whole test file. Injection also lets tests exercise the full
118.  * differ with a Node-safe fake. `definitions/files.tsx` wires the real
119.  * implementation once, at module scope.
120.  */
121. export function makeToRequests({
122.   readFileAsDataURL,
123. }: FileRequestDeps): (
124.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<FileUploadRow>[],
125.   context: StructuredRequestContext,
126. ) => Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
127.   return async function toRequests(edits, { encounterId, questionId }) {
128.     // `requires: ["encounterId", "facilityId"]` on the definition means the
129.     // slot never reaches "ready" without one, so this is unreachable on a
130.     // real submit. Returning before `creates.map` also keeps the injected
131.     // reader from ever running for a context that cannot build a valid
132.     // request.
133.     if (!encounterId) return [];
134.     const { creates } = resolveChanges(edits, {});
135.     return Promise.all(
136.       creates.map(async (row) => {
137.         const base64 = (await readFileAsDataURL(row.file_data)).split(",")[1];
138.         return {
139.           url: `/api/v1/files/upload-file/`,
140.           method: "POST" as const,
141.           body: { ...row, file_data: base64, encounter: encounterId },
142.           reference_id: structuredReferenceId("files", questionId),
143.         };
144.       }),
145.     );
146.   };
147. }

342. export const MEDICATION_REQUEST_SOFT_DELETE: SoftDeleteDescriptor<MedicationRequestRow> =
343.   {
344.     patch: { status: "entered_in_error" },

509.  * A list, not a singleton — like `allergy_intolerance`/`diagnosis`, a row

517. /**
518.  * The edit log → at most one POST against the upsert endpoint, carrying
519.  * every medication this session touched. An empty edit log produces no
520.  * request.
521.  *
522.  * PRESCRIPTION IDENTITY: every row without a server id gets the same
523.  * `alternate_identifier`, generated once per call — new medications saved
524.  * together are grouped under ONE new prescription. Existing rows carry no
525.  * `create_prescription`.
526.  *
527.  * The whole row is spread into the wire body first, then the fields the
528.  * server expects in a different shape are overridden.
529.  */
530. export async function toRequests(
531.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<MedicationRequestRow>[],
532.   { patientId, encounterId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
533. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
534.   if (!patientId) return [];
535.   const { creates, updates, removes } = resolveChanges(edits, {
536.     softDelete: MEDICATION_REQUEST_SOFT_DELETE,
537.   });
538.   const rows = [
539.     ...creates,
540.     ...updates,
541.     ...removes.flatMap((entry) => (entry.row ? [entry.row] : [])),
542.   ];
543.   if (rows.length === 0) return [];
544. 
545.   const prescriptionIdentifier = `${encounterId}-${new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, "-")}`;
546. 
547.   return [
548.     {
549.       url: `/api/v1/patient/${patientId}/medication/request/upsert/`,
550.       method: "POST",
551.       body: {
552.         datapoints: rows.map((row) => ({
553.           ...row,
554.           ...(!row.id && {
555.             create_prescription: {
556.               ...row.create_prescription,
557.               status: PrescriptionStatus.active,
558.               alternate_identifier: prescriptionIdentifier,
559.             },
560.           }),
561.           note: sanitizeNote(row.note),
562.           encounter: encounterId,
563.           patient: patientId,
564.           requester: row.requester?.id,
565.         })),
566.       },
567.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("medication_request", questionId),
568.     },
569.   ];
570. }

572. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
573. // Validation — the per-dosage-instruction nested predicate
574. // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
575. 
576. /** One invalid slot within one medication's dosage instructions. `fieldKey`
577.  *  matches legacy's exact wire convention (`dosage_instruction[i].dose`, and
578.  *  so on) so a future server-side validation error keyed the same way binds
579.  *  to the identical cell. */
580. export interface MedicationRowFieldError {
581.   rowId: string;
582.   fieldKey: string;
583.   /** `"duration"` carries a specific "why it's invalid" reason
584.    *  (`TimingBoundsError`); every other kind reads as a plain required
585.    *  error — mirrors legacy's `validateMedicationRequestQuestion`'s own
586.    *  `field_key?.endsWith(".duration")` branch. */
587.   kind: "required" | "duration";
588.   durationError?: TimingBoundsError;
589. }
590. 
591. function hasValidDose(
592.   instruction: MedicationRequestDosageInstruction,
593. ): boolean {
594.   const doseAndRate = instruction.dose_and_rate;
595.   const doseQuantityValue = doseAndRate?.dose_quantity?.value;
596.   if (doseQuantityValue != null)
597.     return isPositiveDecimalString(doseQuantityValue);
598.   const doseRange = doseAndRate?.dose_range;
599.   if (doseRange) {
600.     return (
601.       isPositiveDecimalString(doseRange.low?.value ?? "0") &&
602.       isPositiveDecimalString(doseRange.high?.value ?? "0")
603.     );
604.   }
605.   return false;
606. }
607. 
608. /**
609.  * A real frequency carries an explicit FHIR timing code, an as-needed flag,
610.  * or a free-text M-A-N pattern. A bare `timing` is not enough — setting a
611.  * duration alone auto-creates a `frequency:1` repeat with no code/text,
612.  * which must not satisfy this.
613.  */
614. function hasValidFrequency(
615.   instruction: MedicationRequestDosageInstruction,
616. ): boolean {
617.   return !!(
618.     instruction.as_needed_boolean ||
619.     instruction.text ||
620.     instruction.timing?.code
621.   );
622. }
623. 
624. /** Duration is optional — only the CONTENTS of a bound that was actually set
625.  *  are validated (range low <= high, period start <= end, ...). Returns the
626.  *  `TimingBoundsError` i18n key, or `null` when there is nothing set or what
627.  *  is set is valid. */
628. function invalidDurationError(
629.   instruction: MedicationRequestDosageInstruction,
630. ): TimingBoundsError | null {
631.   const bounds = localGetTimingBounds(instruction.timing?.repeat);
632.   return bounds ? localValidateTimingBounds(bounds) : null;
633. }
634. 
635. /**
636.  * For every edited (non-removed, non-`entered_in_error`) medication, checks
637.  * each dosage instruction's dose/frequency/duration, producing one
638.  * `MedicationRowFieldError` per invalid slot, index-suffixed to match the
639.  * server's `field_key` convention.
640.  *
641.  * Validates `edits`, not the projection: a row-scoped error needs a `rowId`,
642.  * which only an edit carries. An untouched baseline medication was already
643.  * valid on the server and never blocks Save. `remove` ops and
644.  * `entered_in_error` patches are skipped — a row on its way out must not
645.  * trip validation.
646.  */
647. export function invalidDosageFieldErrors(
648.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<MedicationRequestRow>[],
649. ): MedicationRowFieldError[] {
650.   const errors: MedicationRowFieldError[] = [];
651.   for (const edit of edits) {
652.     if (edit.op === "remove") continue;
653.     const row = edit.patch;
654.     if (row.status === "entered_in_error") continue;
655. 
656.     if (!row.dosage_instruction.length) {
657.       errors.push({
658.         rowId: edit.rowId,
659.         fieldKey: "dosage_instruction",
660.         kind: "required",
661.       });
662.       continue;
663.     }
664. 
665.     row.dosage_instruction.forEach((instruction, index) => {
666.       const keyPrefix = `dosage_instruction[${index}]`;
667.       if (!hasValidDose(instruction)) {
668.         errors.push({
669.           rowId: edit.rowId,
670.           fieldKey: `${keyPrefix}.dose`,
671.           kind: "required",
672.         });
673.       }
674.       if (!hasValidFrequency(instruction)) {
675.         errors.push({
676.           rowId: edit.rowId,
677.           fieldKey: `${keyPrefix}.frequency`,
678.           kind: "required",

1. import { useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
2. 
3. import { PluginErrorBoundary } from "@/components/Common/PluginErrorBoundary";
4. 
5. import {
6.   getFormAssistantsVersion,
7.   listFormAssistants,
8.   subscribeToFormAssistants,
9. } from "./formAssistantRegistry";
10. import type { FillAssistantHandle } from "./types";
11. 
12. /**
13.  * Renders every currently registered `formAssistant` plugin, handing
14.  * each the session's handle. `formAssistant` lives in its own dedicated
15.  * registry (`formAssistantRegistry.ts`), not `SupportedPluginComponents`/
16.  * `PLUGIN_Component`, so this reads that registry directly.
17.  *
18.  * Each assistant is wrapped in its own `PluginErrorBoundary` keyed by its
19.  * TRUSTED registration slug — the backend-issued one `PluginEngine.tsx`
20.  * passed to `registerFormAssistant`, never the manifest's self-declared
21.  * name — so one broken plugin's assistant cannot take the fill canvas
22.  * down with it, and cannot masquerade under another plugin's identity in
23.  * the error log.
24.  */
25. export function FormAssistantSlot({ handle }: { handle: FillAssistantHandle }) {
26.   useSyncExternalStore(
27.     subscribeToFormAssistants,
28.     getFormAssistantsVersion,
29.     getFormAssistantsVersion,
30.   );
31.   const assistants = listFormAssistants();
32.   if (assistants.length === 0) return null;
33.   return (
34.     <>
35.       {assistants.map(({ slug, component: Assistant }) => (
36.         <PluginErrorBoundary key={slug} pluginName={slug}>
37.           <Assistant handle={handle} />
38.         </PluginErrorBoundary>
39.       ))}
40.     </>
41.   );
42. }

1. import { format } from "date-fns";
2. import { z } from "zod";
3. 
4. import { resolveChanges } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/changes";
5. import type {
6.   BaselineRow,
7.   ProjectValues,
8.   SoftDeleteDescriptor,
9. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/core/types";
10. import {
11.   onsetSchema,
12.   userDisplaySchema,
13. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/shared/rowSchemaPrimitives";
14. import type {
15.   StructuredBatchEntry,
16.   StructuredRequestContext,
17. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
18. import { structuredReferenceId } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
19. import { CodeSchema, type Code } from "@/types/base/code/code";
20. import type { Symptom, SymptomRequest } from "@/types/emr/symptom/symptom";
21. import {
22.   SYMPTOM_CLINICAL_STATUS,
23.   SYMPTOM_SEVERITY,
24.   SYMPTOM_VERIFICATION_STATUS,
25. } from "@/types/emr/symptom/symptom";
26. import type { StructuredEdit } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
27. 
28. /** The wire request shape doubles as the editable row shape. */
29. export type SymptomRow = SymptomRequest;
30. 
31. /**
32.  * Assistant write guard. `category` stays a bare non-empty string — no
33.  * exhaustive runtime enum exists for it. Timestamp fields are read-only
34.  * pass-through, left as plain optional strings.
35.  */
36. export const rowSchema = z
37.   .object({
38.     id: z.string().optional(),
39.     clinical_status: z.enum(SYMPTOM_CLINICAL_STATUS),
40.     verification_status: z.enum(SYMPTOM_VERIFICATION_STATUS),
41.     code: CodeSchema,
42.     severity: z.enum(SYMPTOM_SEVERITY),
43.     onset: onsetSchema.optional(),
44.     recorded_date: z.string().optional(),
45.     note: z.string().optional(),
46.     encounter: z.string().min(1),
47.     category: z.string().min(1),
48.     created_date: z.string().optional(),
49.     updated_date: z.string().optional(),
50.     created_by: userDisplaySchema.optional(),
51.   })
52.   .strict();
53. 
54. /**
55.  * Removing a row that exists on the server flips `verification_status` to
56.  * `entered_in_error` and keeps it visible; a row that never reached the
57.  * server is dropped outright. `useStructuredRows` dispatches on this
58.  * descriptor by row origin.
59.  */
60. export const SYMPTOM_SOFT_DELETE: SoftDeleteDescriptor<SymptomRow> = {
61.   patch: { verification_status: "entered_in_error" },
62.   isDeleted: (row) => row.verification_status === "entered_in_error",
63. };
64. 
65. /**
66.  * Read shape → the row this question edits; `onset.onset_datetime` is cut
67.  * down to a bare date. Uses `date-fns` directly — `@/Utils/utils`
68.  * transitively reads `import.meta.env` via `@careConfig`, undefined under
69.  * `node --test`.
70.  */
71. export function toSymptomRow(symptom: Symptom): SymptomRow {
72.   return {
73.     id: symptom.id,
74.     code: symptom.code,
75.     clinical_status: symptom.clinical_status,
76.     verification_status: symptom.verification_status,
77.     severity: symptom.severity,
78.     onset: symptom.onset
79.       ? {
80.           ...symptom.onset,
81.           onset_datetime: symptom.onset.onset_datetime
82.             ? format(new Date(symptom.onset.onset_datetime), "yyyy-MM-dd")
83.             : "",
84.         }
85.       : undefined,
86.     recorded_date: symptom.recorded_date,
87.     note: symptom.note,
88.     category: symptom.category,
89.     encounter: symptom.encounter,
90.     created_date: symptom.created_date,
91.     updated_date: symptom.updated_date,
92.     created_by: symptom.created_by,
93.   };
94. }
95. 
96. /**
97.  * Keyed by the server id so `removeRow` distinguishes baseline
98.  * (soft-delete) from added (annihilate) rows. Callers pass `undefined`,
99.  * never `[]`, while the fetch is unresolved.
100.  */
101. export function toBaselineRows(
102.   symptoms: readonly Symptom[],
103. ): BaselineRow<SymptomRow>[] {
104.   return symptoms.map((symptom) => ({
105.     rowId: symptom.id,
106.     row: toSymptomRow(symptom),
107.   }));
108. }
109. 
110. /** Every symptom this question records is a `problem_list_item`; no
111.  *  control exposes the field. */
112. const SYMPTOM_CATEGORY = "problem_list_item";
113. 
114. /**
115.  * Legacy add-flow defaults: active/confirmed, severity "moderate", onset
116.  * today. `encounter` is set at creation because a row's `patch` must be
117.  * the complete row.
118.  */
119. export function newSymptomRow(code: Code, encounterId: string): SymptomRow {
120.   return {
121.     code,
122.     clinical_status: "active",
123.     verification_status: "confirmed",
124.     severity: "moderate",
125.     category: SYMPTOM_CATEGORY,
126.     onset: { onset_datetime: format(new Date(), "yyyy-MM-dd") },
127.     encounter: encounterId,
128.   };
129. }
130. 
131. /** Duplicate-guard key for `findDuplicateCandidates`, which already
132.  *  excludes soft-deleted (entered_in_error) rows from its seen set. An
133.  *  empty code yields `undefined`, excluding the row from matching. */
134. export function symptomDuplicateKey(row: SymptomRow): string | undefined {
135.   return row.code.code || undefined;
136. }
137. 
138. /** Rows are complete from creation — no empty-row filter needed; an
139.  *  empty list projects to an unanswered section. */
140. export const projectValues: ProjectValues<SymptomRow> = (rows) =>
141.   rows.length === 0 ? [] : [{ type: "symptom", value: [...rows] }];
142. 
143. /**
144.  * Reuses a historical symptom as a NEW row for this encounter: the server
145.  * id is stripped — keeping it would make the upsert update the original
146.  * record in place — and `encounter` is re-stamped to the current
147.  * encounter. Every other field carries over unchanged.
148.  */
149. export function toReusedSymptomRow(
150.   row: SymptomRow,
151.   encounterId: string,
152. ): SymptomRow {
153.   const { id: _id, ...rest } = row;
154.   return { ...rest, encounter: encounterId };
155. }
156. 
157. /** Kept local rather than importing `definitions/adapt.ts`'s
158.  *  `sanitizeNote`: `model.ts` must stay React-free for `node --test`, and
159.  *  adapt.ts imports React. */
160. function sanitizeNote(note: string | undefined): string | undefined {
161.   return note?.trim() || undefined;
162. }
163. 
164. /**
165.  * Edit log → at most one POST to the upsert endpoint. An empty edit log
166.  * yields an empty batch — untouched baseline rows are never re-sent, so a
167.  * concurrent edit to an unrelated symptom cannot be overwritten.
168.  *
169.  * `resolveChanges` receives no baseline: the differ only sees the edit
170.  * log, and the hook's prune effect drops edits for rows the baseline has
171.  * proven gone before submit. A `removes` entry always carries `.row` when
172.  * a softDelete descriptor is supplied; the `flatMap` guard honors the
173.  * shared optional type instead of asserting.
174.  *
175.  * `encounter: encounterId` overrides each row's own value on purpose — a
176.  * reused historical symptom can carry another encounter; re-stamping
177.  * preserves the legacy submit behavior.
178.  */
179. export async function toRequests(
180.   edits: readonly StructuredEdit<SymptomRow>[],
181.   { patientId, encounterId, questionId }: StructuredRequestContext,
182. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
183.   if (!patientId || !encounterId) return [];
184.   const { creates, updates, removes } = resolveChanges(edits, {
185.     softDelete: SYMPTOM_SOFT_DELETE,
186.   });
187.   const rows = [
188.     ...creates,
189.     ...updates,
190.     ...removes.flatMap((entry) => (entry.row ? [entry.row] : [])),
191.   ];
192.   if (rows.length === 0) return [];
193.   return [
194.     {
195.       url: `/api/v1/patient/${patientId}/symptom/upsert/`,
196.       method: "POST",
197.       body: {
198.         datapoints: rows.map((row) => ({
199.           ...row,
200.           note: sanitizeNote(row.note),
201.           encounter: encounterId,
202.         })),
203.       },
204.       reference_id: structuredReferenceId("symptom", questionId),
205.     },
206.   ];
207. }
208.

129. /**

131.  * needs, which questionnaire subjects it may appear on, and whether its
132.  * values are safe to persist in a local draft.

135.   K extends StructuredQuestionType = StructuredQuestionType,

137.   type: K;
138.   component: ComponentType<StructuredInputProps>;

163.  * already had count), while EDITS answer "is what changed well-formed."

1. import type { QuestionnaireResponse } from "@/types/questionnaire/form";
2. import type { StructuredEditRecord } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
3. import { sanitizeStructuredEditLog } from "@/types/questionnaire/structured";
4. 
5. import type {
6.   StructuredBatchEntry,
7.   StructuredRequestContext,
8. } from "@/components/QuestionnaireV2/structured/types";
9. 
10. /**
11.  * A structured question's EDIT LOG — user intent, the only thing that
12.  * compiles into requests and the only thing drafts persist. `undefined`
13.  * (a fresh question, a pre-`edits` draft) reads as an empty log, so
14.  * "nothing changed" and "never touched" are the same thing to every
15.  * consumer.
16.  *
17.  * Hardened because the sources are untrusted JSON — a localStorage draft,
18.  * a server `response_dump` written by another build. Malformed entries
19.  * are dropped rather than thrown on, and duplicates collapse to the last
20.  * one per `rowId`: the "at most one edit per rowId" invariant every
21.  * differ relies on to decide POST-vs-PUT. The sanitization is
22.  * `sanitizeStructuredEditLog` (`types/questionnaire/structured.ts`) — the
23.  * SAME ingestion-boundary gate `structured/core/useStructuredRows.ts`
24.  * runs its own `response.edits` through, so a malformed log is reduced to
25.  * a well-formed one before EITHER the projection (`projectRows`) or the
26.  * submit compiler (`resolveChanges`, via `toRequests` below) ever sees
27.  * it.
28.  *
29.  * Lives here rather than in `structured/registry.ts` because
30.  * `registry.ts` transitively imports every core structured definition's
31.  * real component tree (CSS, UI libraries) and cannot run under the plain
32.  * `node --test` harness this module exists to be tested under.
33.  * `composeBatch.ts` and `validateStructured.ts` import it from here.
34.  */
35. export function structuredEditsOf(
36.   response: QuestionnaireResponse | undefined,
37. ): StructuredEditRecord[] {
38.   return sanitizeStructuredEditLog(response?.edits);
39. }
40. 
41. /**
42.  * What `composeStructuredV2Requests` needs from a resolved structured
43.  * type — a structural subset of `ResolvedStructuredType`
44.  * (`structured/registry.ts`) / `StructuredTypeDefinition`
45.  * (`structured/types.ts`), duck-typed rather than imported so this module
46.  * stays import-free of `registry.ts` (see `structuredEditsOf`'s doc
47.  * comment) and is exercisable under plain `node --test`. Every real
48.  * definition — core or plugin — satisfies this structurally, so
49.  * `composeBatch.ts` passes its resolved definition straight through with
50.  * no cast.
51.  */
52. export interface StructuredV2Compiler {
53.   toRequests: (
54.     edits: readonly StructuredEditRecord[],
55.     context: StructuredRequestContext,
56.   ) => Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]>;
57. }
58. 
59. /**
60.  * The v2 leg of `composeBatch`'s structured compile step, extracted as a
61.  * pure function so it is unit-testable under `node --test` (`composeBatch.ts`
62.  * itself imports `structured/registry.ts`, which is not runnable there —
63.  * see `structuredEditsOf`'s doc comment).
64.  *
65.  * Only what the clinician CHANGED reaches `toRequests` — the projection
66.  * (the patient's existing rows, `values[0].value`) is display state and
67.  * never reaches a domain endpoint, so an untouched section cannot
68.  * re-upsert anything.
69.  * Short-circuits on an empty log WITHOUT calling `toRequests` at all, so
70.  * the guarantee holds even for a type whose own `toRequests` is not
71.  * itself empty-safe.
72.  */
73. export async function composeStructuredV2Requests(
74.   definition: StructuredV2Compiler,
75.   response: QuestionnaireResponse,
76.   context: StructuredRequestContext,
77. ): Promise<StructuredBatchEntry[]> {
78.   const edits = structuredEditsOf(response);
79.   if (edits.length === 0) return [];
80.   return definition.toRequests(edits, context);
81. }
82.

84.   return (
85.     a.open === b.open &&
86.     a.date === b.date &&

121.     // `scheduleServiceTypeAtom` sets `getOnInit: true`, this first read

157.   const handleSlotDetailsChange = useCallback(

32.  * `ManageResponseTemplatesSheet.tsx`'s `handleApplyTemplate` relies on to
33.  * skip its "applied" checkmark animation and clear `applyingTemplateId`
34.  * through its `catch` block: the template has nothing of this type
35.  * (`items` empty/absent), or every item failed to resolve. A partial
36.  * success does NOT throw — it returns the rows that DID resolve, with a
37.  * warning toast naming the shortfall.
38.  *
39.  * Adds nothing anywhere itself — the caller commits the returned rows via
40.  * ONE `list.addRows(rows)` call, never a loop of `list.addRow`: two
41.  * mutator calls issued synchronously in the same handler read the same
42.  * stale `edits` snapshot (see `useStructuredRows.ts`), so a loop would
43.  * silently drop every row but the last.
44.  */

46.   items: readonly TSpec[] | undefined,
47.   resolve: (spec: TSpec) => Promise<TRow>,
48.   templateName: string,
49.   messages: ApplyTemplateItemsMessages,

51.   if (!items?.length) {
52.     toast.info(t(messages.empty));
53.     throw new Error("Template has no items of this type");
54.   }

1. import { z } from "zod";
2. 
3. /**
4.  * Shared building blocks for every type's `rowSchema`
5.  * (`fill/assistant/structuredEditValidation.ts`'s `rowSchemaOf` contract:
6.  * `.strict()` schemas, so unknown fields are rejected rather than silently
7.  * stripped).
8.  *
9.  * Dependency-free by the same rule every `model.ts` here follows: no
10.  * `@careConfig`-touching import, directly or transitively — `npm run
11.  * test:unit` is plain `node --import tsx --test`, where `import.meta.env`
12.  * is `undefined`. `zod` itself is safe.
13.  *
14.  * NOT a re-implementation of `fill/assistant/coercion.ts`'s date coercion —
15.  * that module coerces a PLAIN ANSWER's raw string; this one validates a
16.  * STRUCTURED ROW field. The round-trip rigor (rebuild a `Date` from parsed
17.  * components and require an exact match) is deliberately the same shape,
18.  * because the hazard is identical: `new Date("2024-02-31")` silently
19.  * becomes March 2 wherever a calendar date string is accepted from outside
20.  * the type's own UI.
21.  */
22. 
23. /** A real calendar date, strictly `YYYY-MM-DD` — matches every onset/last-
24.  *  occurrence/authored-on-date field across the ported types. Rejects
25.  *  `"2024-02-31"` (not a real day), a 2-digit year, and any non-ISO
26.  *  separator/format, not just a malformed shape. */
27. export const dateOnlyString = z.string().refine(
28.   (value) => {
29.     const match = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(value);
30.     if (!match) return false;
31.     const [, y, m, d] = match;
32.     const year = Number(y);
33.     const month = Number(m);
34.     const day = Number(d);
35.     const date = new Date(0);
36.     date.setFullYear(year, month - 1, day);
37.     return (
38.       date.getFullYear() === year &&
39.       date.getMonth() === month - 1 &&
40.       date.getDate() === day
41.     );
42.   },
43.   { message: "must be a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format" },
44. );
45. 
46. /** A timezone-aware instant — anything `new Date(...)` parses to a real
47.  *  time (rejects `""`, whitespace, and any string `Date.parse` cannot
48.  *  resolve). Deliberately looser than {@link dateOnlyString}: every
49.  *  consumer of this (`authored_on`, `effective_period.start/end`,
50.  *  `deceased_datetime`) stores a full ISO instant produced by a picker
51.  *  (`Date.toISOString()`/`DateTimeInput`), not a hand-typed date-only
52.  *  string, so the rollover hazard `dateOnlyString` guards against does not
53.  *  apply the same way here — there is no "day 31 of a 30-day month"
54.  *  ambiguity in a full timestamp the way there is in a bare calendar date. */
55. export const isoInstantString = z
56.   .string()
57.   .min(1)
58.   .refine((value) => !Number.isNaN(new Date(value).getTime()), {
59.     message: "must be a valid date-time string",
60.   });
61. 
62. /** A non-blank string — `z.string().min(1)` named for what it guards
63.  *  against (an assistant patch setting a required text field to `""`),
64.  *  reused across every type whose row has a required free-text/id field. */
65. export const nonEmptyString = z.string().min(1);
66. 
67. /**
68.  * A DISPLAY object a row carries alongside the id it actually submits —
69.  * `UserReadMinimal` (`requester`/`performer_actor_object`), a picked
70.  * definition (`charge_item_definition_object`/`activity_definition_object`),
71.  * a product (`requested_product_internal`). Deliberately `.loose()`,
72.  * not `.strict()`, and this is the one documented exception to the
73.  * "unknown fields rejected" rule every OTHER field in every `rowSchema`
74.  * follows: these are large, purely-informational READ shapes (tens of
75.  * optional fields across nested billing/category/tag types) an assistant
76.  * would only ever COPY VERBATIM from a prior lookup the host already
77.  * performed, never author field-by-field from a voice command. Requiring
78.  * exact strictness here would force this schema to duplicate the FULL
79.  * shape of `UserReadMinimal`/`ChargeItemDefinitionRead`/
80.  * `ActivityDefinitionReadSpec` (none of them "shapes worth an assistant
81.  * hand-typing") for a security property (typo/hallucination rejection)
82.  * that only matters for fields an author actually TYPES. `id` is required
83.  * because every real consumer of these objects keys off it (equality
84.  * checks, the `UserSelector`/definition pickers); the rest of
85.  * `requiredStringKeys` names whatever ELSE this call site's own row-level
86.  * code actually reads off the object directly (e.g. a definition's
87.  * `slug`/`title`) — everything not named is only checked for PRESENCE via
88.  * `.loose()`, never for an exhaustive key list.
89.  */
90. export function displayObjectSchema(
91.   extraRequiredStringKeys: readonly string[] = [],
92. ) {
93.   const shape: Record<string, z.ZodType> = { id: nonEmptyString };
94.   for (const key of extraRequiredStringKeys) shape[key] = nonEmptyString;
95.   return z.object(shape).loose();

/**
 * A projection-only write for a structured question's `values` mirror —
 * deliberately skips {@link clearQuestionErrorsInState}, unlike
 * {@link useQuestionResponse}'s setter.
 *
 * `useStructuredRows` writes a question's response from two kinds of
 * event. A mutator records real intent — clearing the question's prior
 * errors on that write is correct, and those writes go through
 * `useQuestionResponse`'s setter. But it also mirrors `baseline + edits`
 * into `values` on every baseline movement (first load, refetch, cache
 * invalidation) via a passive effect that records no new intent; routing
 * that through the intent setter would let a background refetch silently
 * clear a showing submit-time server error while the offending value
 * stayed on screen. This setter writes `values` alone and leaves
 * `errorsAtom` untouched, so only genuine user (or seed) intent ever
 * clears a question's errors.
 *
 * Scoped to `values` (never `edits`) on purpose — a passive mirror of
 * baseline movement must never touch the edit log, which is the one thing
 * drafts persist and submit reads.
 */

/**
 * A projection-only write for a structured question's `values` mirror —
 * deliberately skips {@link clearQuestionErrorsInState}, unlike

 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS (master plan "Carry-forwards out of Phase 1" item 2 /
 * design annex `docs/superpowers/specs/annexes/p1-state-core.md` §10).
 * `structured/core/useStructuredRows.ts` writes this question's response
 * from two different kinds of event: a MUTATOR (`applyEdit`/`addRow`/
 * `updateRow`/`removeRow`/`setRow`/`clearRow`, the orphan-prune effect, the
 * `initialEdits` seed) records real intent — clearing this question's
 * prior errors on that write is correct, same as every other question
 * type, and those all go through `useQuestionResponse`'s setter
 * unchanged. But `useStructuredRows` ALSO mirrors `baseline + edits` into
 * `values` on every baseline movement (first load, refetch, cache
 * invalidation) via a passive effect that records no new intent at all —
 * before this setter existed, that effect had no choice but to reuse
 * `useQuestionResponse`'s setter too, so a background refetch landing
 * while a submit-time server error was showing on this question would
 * silently clear that error while the offending value stayed on screen
 * unchanged, letting the clinician believe the problem was resolved. This
 * setter is the fix: a PASSIVE projection refresh writes `values` alone
 * and leaves `errorsAtom` untouched, so only genuine user (or seed) intent
 * ever clears a question's errors.
 *
 * Scoped to `values` alone (never `edits`) on purpose — nothing that only
 * mirrors baseline movement should ever be able to touch the edit log,
 * which is the one thing drafts persist and submit reads.
 */
